rationales: There are more than eight types in the standard classification of solutions.
Solutions are classified into nine types based on the physical states of solute and solvent.
Seven is not the standard number of solution types.
Ten is not the standard number of solution types.
Oxygen is a substance, not a solution by itself.
Carbon dioxide is a compound, not a solution by itself.
Air is a homogeneous mixture of gases and is a solution.
Nitrogen is a substance, not a solution by itself.
HF is not ionic; its atoms share electrons.
HF is polar because fluorine attracts the shared electrons more strongly than hydrogen.
HF does not form its bond by donation of a lone pair to an electron-deficient atom.
HF has a polar covalent bond because its electrons are shared unequally.
Donation of electrons is associated with forming ionic bonds, not covalent bonds.
Acceptance of electrons is associated with forming ionic bonds, not covalent bonds.
A covalent bond forms when atoms share electrons.
Repulsion of electrons does not form a covalent bond.
Alkali metals are Group 1 elements, not d-block elements.
Halogens are Group 17 elements, not d-block elements.
d-block elements are generally called transition metals.
Alkaline earth metals are Group 2 elements, not d-block elements.
Rutherford proposed a nuclear model but did not use the concept of quantized orbits.
Planck introduced the quantum theory, not the planetary orbit model of the atom.
Bohr used the concept of fixed orbits for electrons around the nucleus.
J. J. Thomson proposed the plum-pudding model, not the orbit model.
NaCl is the chemical formula of common salt.
CaC₂ is calcium carbide, not common salt.
SiO₂ is silicon dioxide, not common salt.
CaO is calcium oxide, not common salt.
Sulphur is generally dull, not lustrous.
Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
Phosphorus is generally not lustrous.
Carbon is not the standard example of a lustrous non-metal in this context.
Ether is not called the universal solvent.
Water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves many substances.
Sodium carbonate is a solute, not the universal solvent.
Sulphur is not called the universal solvent.
Alcohol mixes with water.
Sugar dissolves in water.
Sodium carbonate is soluble in water.
Petrol does not dissolve in water.
Tin's transition temperature is about 13.2°C, not 12.2°C.
Tin changes between white and grey forms at about 13.2°C.
14.2°C is not the standard transition temperature of tin.
15.2°C is not the standard transition temperature of tin.
Eight is oxygen's atomic number, not the mass number of its common isotope.
Eight is the atomic number of oxygen, not its common mass number.
Twelve is not the mass number of the common oxygen isotope.
The common isotope oxygen-16 has a mass number of 16.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among the halogens.
Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine and iodine.
Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
Iodine has the lowest electronegativity among these halogens.
CH₄ contains only single covalent bonds.
C₂H₄ contains a double covalent bond.
C₂H₂ contains a carbon–carbon triple covalent bond.
C₂H₆ contains only single covalent bonds.
NH₃ has a complete octet around nitrogen.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons around it in the molecule.
N₂ has a triple bond and complete octets on both nitrogen atoms.
O₂ has a double bond and complete octets on both oxygen atoms.
